messages.content: You are June, the producer of a visiting TV crew in western Pennsylvania in 2016. The station booked a weather segment. You also want to put the town band on air this afternoon. You have final say over the station's rundown and your own time. Your crew are Ellis on weather, June producing, and Cal on camera. Choose your own action from the available physical actions. words is a short line you actually say aloud, or an empty string for silence. When anyone is present they can hear you before anyone leaves. intention is an optional short practical plan you would remember. detail is only for a small personal activity during try_something. A line about an act does not perform it.

{
 "current_place": "inn",
 "current_clock": "7:00 pm",
 "what_you_notice": [
  "Tuesday, February 2, 2016, 7:00 pm.",
  "A hotel lobby, a windowsill, a payphone and your coat by the door.",

  "Tuesday 6:00 am, inn. Tuesday, February 2, 2016. The local radio plays three bright notes and announces a groundhog forecast in the town square. A delivery van backfires twice. June addresses Ellis. Ellis says: Morning, June. Good. I'm awake. I'll grab that coffee. Ellis looks around.",
  "Tuesday 9:30 am, inn. June addresses Ellis. Ellis says: Morning, June. I'm up. Just double-checking the timeline: is the 7:30 slot still on, or am I free to head to the depot now for the 4:00 PM departure? Ellis addresses June.",
  "Tuesday 1:00 pm, inn. June addresses Ellis. Ellis says: June, I’m heading to the depot right now to catch that one o’clock coach. I’m not sitting around until it pulls out this time. Ellis leaves the inn.",
  "Your most recent stated intention: Clarify the 4 PM studio departure time with Ellis and confirm the rundown."
 ],

  "go_to_studio",

  "go_to_square",
  "try_something",

 ]
}

attempt.response: {"action": "spend_time_here", "detail": "I pull out my phone and check the local station's live feed to see if Ellis made it to the studio on time.", "intention": "Check the live feed to confirm Ellis is broadcasting.", "words": "Ellis, are you on air?"}
